Subject: RFI: Throughput validation and surge-replay methodology

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our procurement RFI we need a clear, machine-verifiable description of how Redwood validates throughput and tail-latency under real-world surge conditions. The RFP appendix attached has our expected deliverables but we want a short, runnable plan from you that covers: 
- How you replay customer traffic (formats accepted, fidelity guarantees)
- What measurement matrix you capture (P50/P95/P99, CPU/GPU utilization, memory, kernel-level counters)
- Cold-start vs warm-path separation and how you isolate cache effects
- How fallbacks and multi-variant routing affect observed latency and throughput numbers
- Testbed specs (GPU type, quantization used, batcher config) and run reproducibility notes

Primary ask: please return a single document with the protocol and an example measurement matrix so we can compare vendor results across our vendors. We attached the RFP annex.

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear asks and the annex. Attached is a concise protocol we follow internally (redwood-surge-replay-protocol-v1.docx). High-level summary here so you can triage quickly: 

Summary (TL;DR):
- Replay method: we accept structured request logs (JSON lines) and HTTP captures (HAR/pcap). We run a replay harness that preserves original inter-arrival times or performs accelerated wall-clock replay (configurable).
- Measurement matrix: we capture per-request timing (enqueue, dequeue, scheduling, model step, token generation), P50/P90/P95/P99, per-shard GPU utilization, CUDA kernel timings, memory high-water marks, and KV-cache hit rates.
- Cold vs warm: two-stage runs. Warm runs (10m steady-state) to populate KV/prefix caches; cold runs sample new model instances with deliberate zero-cache initial traffic to show worst-case. We report both and provide guidance on SLOs tied to warm-path metrics.
- Fallback impact: our runner can toggle fallback behaviors (regional reroute, lower-quant model variant, CPU-based soft-fallback) and we produce separate matrices for each policy.
- Testbed: we include explicit machine specs (GPU model, driver, CU config), exact model binary (hash), quantization profile, and batcher config so results are reproducible.

Deliverables we will provide if you choose Redwood: 
1) Protocol doc (attached) with commands and flags to reproduce
2) A run artifact package: raw replay input, runner config, metrics CSV, flamegraphs for the hot-paths
3) Canary run using your sample logs (we can run in our dedicated sandbox or provide the runner to you)

Next steps: please share either a small sample of your production traces (1k requests) or confirm you want Redwood to replay from the annex's synthetic traffic model.

I attached the protocol and a canary-run template. Happy to set a 30-min alignment call this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: redwood-surge-replay-protocol-v1.docx; canary-run-log-template.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: FW: RFI: Throughput validation and surge-replay methodology

Internal — looping you both in to coordinate the Sensorlytics ask (deal RWF-2026-724). Priya requested a single runnable protocol + example matrix. Action items below.

Action (Ben): please prep a short canary job config that uses our public "synth-sensor-model" (fp16 quantized) and an additional run using a 4-bit quantized variant. Produce P50/P90/P95/P99 and per-shard GPU kernel traces. Use the dedicated-qa-32g cluster (A100s) and include exact CUDA/cuDNN versions. Target: first-pass artifact within 48 hours.

Action (Karthik): confirm the fallback policy permutations to include in the public matrix — recommended: (1) full model, (2) quantized fallback, (3) regional reroute fallback. Also add note about how we mark requests that hit KV-cache vs miss.

Testing notes:
- Replay harness: use --preserve-arrival-times and produce an accelerated run at 5x wall-clock as an option.
- Cold starts: schedule 5 cold workers per run and rotate to create realistic variance.
- Metrics export: prometheus histogram buckets must map to our CSV columns (tokenized timing steps).

Priya asked for reproducibility. We'll include the exact binary hash and a docker image containing the runner. Keep output in the canonical artifact layout so it can be handed back as evidence.

Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the protocol and the quick internal coordination note. This looks aligned with what our benchmarking team expects. A few clarifications before we hand this to our bench squad: 

1) For warm-path reporting: do you provide a steady-state window delta (e.g., minutes 5–10) so we can compare across vendors on identical windows?
2) For fallback permutations, can you include the exact config flags you used (so our runners can toggle them identically)?
3) Will you accept a scrubbed 1k-request sample in JSONL (no PII) for us to drop into your sandbox, or do you prefer we transfer a HAR/pcap?

We will provide a scrubbed JSONL (ETA 72 hours). Also please confirm acceptance criteria we should use when evaluating (suggested: P95 < 280ms warm, P99 < 950ms warm on A100-80config but open to Redwood's recommended SLOs).

If you can confirm the steady-state window and that you will produce the runner flags in the document, we can schedule the bench run next Tue.

Thanks,
Priya
